withholding.name: Comptroller of Maryland, Revenue Administration Division

ui.name: Maryland Department of Labor, Division of Unemployment Insurance

efile.text: Filing your withholding return electronically is now the default option for employers. If you are submitting 25 or more W-2 or 1099 forms you are required to file electronically.

returns.name: Form MW506, Employer's Return of Income Tax Withheld (MW506M for accelerated filers)
contents: Quarterly withholding returns are due the 15th day of the month that follows the calendar quarter; annual filers file the MW506 by the last day of January; accelerated filers file the MW506M within three business days of the pay date and enter the pay date on it.
The employer remains responsible when a third party files or pays, and must provide each employee a W-2 by January 31.

returns.name: Form MW508, Annual Employer Withholding Reconciliation Return
contents: Due January 31 with the state copy of every W-2 or 1099 showing Maryland tax withheld.

25 or more W-2s or 1099s must be filed electronically: bulk-file a modified-Maryland-format text file (SSA Publication 42-007 / IRS Publication 1220) as a Maryland Tax Connect user, upload as a registered Transmitter User, or key fewer than 25 in the portal.
Maryland cannot process the Combined Federal/State program.

notModelled: Where an accelerated filer's quarter-end remainder under $700 is paid: the statute and regulation do not say; the quarterly return date is used.

deposits.interpretation: Maryland has five filing categories. ACCELERATED: an employer that withheld $15,000 or more in the preceding calendar year and has $700 or more of accumulated withholding must remit within three business days following the payroll (pay date; the date paychecks are made available to employees), on Form MW506M; a waiver allowing monthly returns can be requested and renewed. MONTHLY: $700 or more of withholding expected in a quarter (the Comptroller's 2024 guide words it 'more than $700'). QUARTERLY: less than $700 of withholding per quarter; quarterly returns are due the 15th day of the month that follows the quarter. ANNUAL: less than $250 withholding per calendar year; the annual Form MW506 is due the last day of January following the year. SEASONAL: only with prior approval (not modelled). INTERPRETATIONS: (1) the $700 accelerated test is applied to the tax accumulated and not yet paid since the last payment, evaluated at each pay date and restarting each quarter; the remainder under $700 at quarter end is paid with the quarterly return date (the guide does not say where it goes). (2) The MONTHLY return is due the 15th of the following month (COMAR 03.04.01.01(D)(3), read from the State's regulation); the statute and regulation say a person who expects $700 or MORE in a quarter files monthly, while the Comptroller's 2024 guide says 'more than $700': the statute is followed. The category is assigned by the Comptroller, so the frequency is an INPUT; the look-back derivation uses the $15,000 prior-year test only for accelerated, and only when the quarterly amount is also supplied, so the engine does not derive it. The rules above are confirmed against Tax-General 10-822 and COMAR 03.04.01.01 (source S3), which state the accelerated trigger as accumulated tax that 'equals or exceeds $700' after any payroll.

lookback.description: None: the category depends on both the prior-year total and the quarterly amount

channels.function: withholding returns and payments, MW508, W-2/1099 bulk or transmitter filing
channels.description: Maryland Tax Connect (mdtaxconnect.gov): electronic filing and payment is the default; a Transmitter User may upload W-2/1099 files; reporting agents are authorized on Form 548P
enrollment: Register with Maryland (Central Registration number) and create a Maryland Tax Connect login with the withholding account.

A third-party reporting agent obtains information and acts on a client's withholding returns and payments under Form 548P, Limited Power of Attorney and Maryland Reporting Agents Authorization, which Maryland uses instead of the federal Form 8655.
To upload W-2/1099 files for clients, register as a Transmitter User on Maryland Tax Connect.
channels.specs: The modified Maryland standard format for W-2/1099 text files is in the Comptroller's Employer Reporting instructions (not read); contact efileW21099help@marylandtaxes.gov for bulk-file technical support.

returns.name: Quarterly contribution and wage report and UI tax payment
contents: Payroll is reported and UI taxes paid within one month of quarter end: April 30, July 31, October 31 and January 31; a Saturday or Sunday moves the date to the next business day.
Interest is charged at 1.5% a month on late payments (guide).

notModelled: The guide's rule names Saturday and Sunday only; whether a holiday moves the date is not stated, so holidays are treated as moving it.
The guide's edition date is not printed in the text read.
